products.name: Nitecore NU25 MCT UL 400 Lumen USB-C Rechargeable Ultralight Headlamp, 3 color temperatures
specs: 1.65 oz (47 g) with elastic cord headband
About 2 h 40 min at 400 lm, about 13 h at 60 lm, up to 45 h at 6 lm
3000 K warm, 4500 K neutral, 6500 K cool, plus red (low, high, slow flash)
products.warranty: Nitecore covers lighting products with a built-in battery for 24 months, then offers limited lifetime support that covers labor only.
products.returns: Nitecore Store: ask for a return authorization within 15 days of delivery, then ship the item back within the next 15 days. Non-defective returns carry a 15% restocking fee unless an agent waives it. If the order shipped free, the original shipping cost comes out of the refund.
products.summary: A 47 g (1.65 oz) headlamp with a 400-lumen max, three color temperatures, a red light, USB-C charging and IP66 sealing.
products.fit: Best for thru-hikers, ultralight backpackers and trail runners who want a real trail light at the lowest practical weight.
caveats: High lasts only about 2 h 40 min. Plan to use the 60-lumen mode, or carry a small power bank.
Testers call the thin cord headband less comfortable over long hours, and say it can twist.
The two-button interface takes practice, and the small buttons are hard to press with gloves.
The sealed battery can't be replaced, so a worn cell means a new lamp.
You can't use it while it charges.

products.name: Nitecore NU25 MCT 400 Lumen USB-C Rechargeable Headlamp with standard headband, 3 color temperatures
specs: Up to 45 h at the lowest setting
products.warranty: Nitecore covers lighting products with a built-in battery for 24 months, then offers limited lifetime support that covers labor only.
products.returns: Nitecore Store: ask for a return authorization within 15 days of delivery, then ship the item back within the next 15 days. Non-defective returns carry a 15% restocking fee unless an agent waives it.
products.summary: The same 400-lumen lamp as the NU25 MCT UL, with a wider fabric headband instead of the elastic cord. It weighs 3 g more.
products.fit: Best for hikers who wear the light for hours and found cord headbands uncomfortable.
caveats: Same short high-mode runtime and sealed battery as the UL version.
It weighs 3 g more than the UL version.

products.name: Nitecore NU20 Classic 360 Lumen USB-C Lightweight Headlamp with red and high-CRI reading light
specs: 1.34 oz (38 g) with bracket and headband
Main white, red, high-CRI (90+) 4500 K reading light
products.warranty: Nitecore covers lighting products with a built-in battery for 24 months, then offers limited lifetime support that covers labor only.
products.returns: Nitecore Store: ask for a return authorization within 15 days of delivery, then ship the item back within the next 15 days. Non-defective returns carry a 15% restocking fee unless an agent waives it.
products.summary: A 38 g headlamp with a 360-lumen max, a red light, a high-CRI reading light, USB-C charging and IP66 sealing.
products.fit: Best for budget gram-counters and for hikers who mostly use a headlamp for camp chores.
caveats: Packstack found turbo drops from 360 to about 200 lumens within roughly 30 minutes.
It has a smaller 500 mAh battery than the NU25, and it is sealed in.
It has no mode memory and always starts on low. Owners also flag the thin plastic bracket as a wear point.

notes: Query choice: 'best ultralight headlamp for backpacking'. The search results are thin: mostly spammy roundups (pages.dev sites, foliumbiosciences), forum threads and single-product reviews. Pain points across the sources read: short runtime on high, 5 (Treeline, Packstack, BLF/r/Ultralight test, BPL forum x2). Cord or headband comfort and tangling, 4 (r/Ultralight author, Treeline, Packstack citing Live for the Outdoors 3/5 comfort and The Trek, Packstack NU20). Confusing UI, small buttons or no mode memory, 4 (Treeline, Packstack, r/Ultralight, Packstack NU20). Non-replaceable battery, 3 (Packstack x2, BPL). Bindi micro-USB port, 3 (r/Ultralight author, commenter, CleverHiker). Low mode not low enough or no firefly mode, 3 (r/Ultralight author, commenter, BPL). Segments: UL backpacker/thru-hiker -> NU25 MCT UL (400 lm, 47 g, USB-C, IP66, $36.95). Budget or lowest weight with real output -> NU20 Classic (38 g, 360 lm, $24.95). The Bindi is lightest at 35 g but has 200 lm, micro-USB and IPX4. Comfort -> NU25 MCT on a fabric band (50 g, $39.95). No-recharge long stretches -> BD Spot 400 (AAA, IPX8); no Amazon record per the temporary rule, maker URL only. Verified on the Nitecore Store via storecheck on 2026-11-10: prices, availability, URLs, NU25 MCT UL weight (1.65 oz), NU25 MCT weight (1.76 oz), 400 lm, 45 h at the lowest setting. storecheck.py product returned HTTP 429 every time, so I could not read variants (colors); search results did give price and availability. Nitecore's own NU25 MCT UL product page returned 404. The 2 h 40 min at 400 lm, 13 h at 60 lm, IP66, 75-minute charge and 132 m figures come from the Treeline and Packstack pages, which I read; Decathlon's listing matches. NU20 Classic specs come from nitecore.com (read). Its turbo step-down and 2 h turbo figure come from Packstack (read). Bindi specs: CleverHiker (read) and the r/Ultralight test; petzl.com returned 404 to direct fetch. The 680 mAh battery and 4 h charge come from a search summary of petzl.com and are not otherwise confirmed. BD Spot 400: blackdiamondequipment.com returned 429. Weight, IPX8 and AAA come from Treeline (read), whose weight figures disagree with each other (72 g vs 2.7 oz). Not verified, so I printed no Spot 400 price, runtime or exact AAA weight. The r/Ultralight sphere test covered the older NU25 UL (non-MCT), and the page says so. Warranty: nitecore.com lists 24 months for lighting with a built-in battery. Returns: 15-day RMA window with a 15% restocking fee, from the store's refund policy (read). Codes: 10OFF (Awin) applies sitewide. UTL19 (Awin and the brand-site banner, 20% off the UTL19, ends 2026-11-12) applies to no recorded product, so I left it out. The store banner's link points to a 'UTL29' discount URL, which doesn't match the code. A newsletter offers 10% off a first order, with no code shown. Not cart-tested.
